cities.name: New Wobbleton
cities.desc: Capital of Wobbleland, where the Council of Cities meets and the Seagull Guardians keep watch. Home to a fragment of the Great Cauldron and the island's main train hub. Known for its clock towers and endless arguments over the syrup tax.

holidays.title: The Great Wobble Day
holidays.desc: Giant swaying platforms are built on Seagull Square; residents compete to stand longest holding a cup of coffee for the title of "Wobble Master"; seagulls march the main street and get bread treats.

holidays.title: New Year
holidays.desc: Taverns serve gooseberry wine; seagulls take places of honor at the tables; children share sweet pies with the birds by the bonfires.

dishes.name: Clocktower Stew
dishes.desc: Meat-and-vegetable stew slow-cooked and served in small pots with clock-shaped lids.

dishes.name: Seagull's Bite Pastry
dishes.desc: Fish-and-lemon pastries so fragrant that seagulls try to steal them.

streets.name: Seagull Square
streets.desc: The main square, where all city life converges.

streets.name: Yesterday's Tomorrow Street
streets.desc: Home to the club of messenger hens.

streets.name: Falling Up Rock Street
streets.desc: Site of the 24-hour fuel station.

residents.name: Mr. Chew
residents.note: Originally from Snailhollow, Mossy Shell Lane 3.

cities.neighbors: Sits between LemonVale and Snailhollow, across the Ripple Tickle Sea from Noodleford.

cities.name: Maplewink
cities.desc: A maple-syrup town where mornings begin with a wink over a cup of maple coffee. Its economy runs on maple syrup and small craft workshops. Famous for its golden-leaf autumn season and deep reverence for bees, whose honey syrup is prized as highly as maple.

holidays.title: Hivekeeper's Eve
holidays.desc: Residents leave wax candles by the beehives to thank the bees; a gift of homemade honey cookies is considered a blessing for the year.

holidays.title: The Great Wink Day
holidays.desc: Everyone winks at their neighbor over maple coffee; a "Winking Marathon" is held; free syrup of unusual flavors is poured; evening street concerts.

holidays.title: The Fall of Leaves Festival
holidays.desc: Leaf fights, a contest for the pancake that looks most like a fallen leaf, and a giant pancake filling the main square, drenched in syrup.

holidays.title: Amber Night
holidays.desc: The city is lit with amber lamps; residents drink hot mead and syrup drinks and tell tales of giant bees.

dishes.name: Maple-Soaked Pancakes
dishes.desc: Fluffy pancakes served swimming in maple syrup.

streets.name: Pancake Lane
streets.desc: Morning-breakfast and evening-pancake street with live music.

streets.name: Golden Sap Square
streets.desc: Central square hosting the syrup fairs.

cities.neighbors: East of Noodleford and the Syrup Factory, at the far edge of the sea.

cities.name: Snailhollow
cities.desc: A slow-paced, moss-covered town where nothing is ever rushed; snails of every size roam the streets, some large enough for children to ride. Home to Mr. Chew and Detective Titos.

holidays.title: Slowstep Festival
holidays.desc: Residents compete to walk the length of a street as slowly as possible without stopping; herbalists and bakers offer honeyed snail teas; children decorate snails with ribbons for a parade.

dishes.name: Mossy Tea
dishes.desc: Mild, faintly sweet herbal tea with mint and forest moss.

dishes.name: Slow-Baked Honey Bread
dishes.desc: Bread baked for a full day, moist and sweet with honey.

streets.name: Mossy Shell Lane
streets.desc: Green, moss-covered lane where local snails parade.

streets.name: Slowstep Street
streets.desc: Street where even the lamps are lit unhurriedly.

cities.neighbors: Wraps around Mossy Lake, just north of New Wobbleton and Jamshire.

cities.name: Pinecrust
cities.desc: A forest bakery town smelling of pine and fresh pastry, famous for its crisp nut-crust pies and its Festival of Pies Under the Pines.

holidays.title: Festival of Pies Under the Pines
holidays.desc: Long tables of pies fill the streets; tradition is to give the first slice to a neighbor or stranger; pie-shaped lanterns are lit at dusk.

holidays.title: Day of Squirrel Bakers
holidays.desc: Children dress as squirrels and "baked nuts"; a contest for the best nut pie, winner gets a golden pinecone; legend says squirrels help bake that day.

holidays.title: Festival of Warm Ovens
holidays.desc: Bakers compete to keep their pastries hot the longest; residents bring mittens to warm their hands; the evening ends with communal tea and icing-decorated pastries.

dishes.name: Pine Nut Pie
dishes.desc: Nut pie with an extra-crisp crust.

dishes.name: Forest Brew
dishes.desc: Tea made from young pine needles and forest berries.

dishes.name: Crispy Squirrel Loaf
dishes.desc: Nut-heavy bread, a nod to the squirrel-baker legend.

streets.name: Nutmeg Hollow Road
streets.desc: Smells of fresh pastry and pine forest.

streets.name: Pinecone Alley
streets.desc: Where children hold pinecone fights.

streets.name: Crisp Crust Street
streets.desc: Street of bakeries and pie shops.

cities.neighbors: Tucked into the Nut Forest, south of Cheddarford and west of Kettleford.

cities.name: LemonVale
cities.desc: A fertile valley built entirely around lemons — used in soups, pies, candles, and decoration; the old local currency was called "wedges." Famously hospitable; no traveler leaves hungry.

holidays.title: Festival of Lemon Drops
holidays.desc: Lemon-drop candies are handed out on the square; children play "Catch the Wedge"; adults boil syrup.

holidays.title: Festival of Lemon Lights
holidays.desc: The city is decorated with candied lemon-peel garlands; a contest for "sourest lemon."

holidays.title: Lantern Lemon Night
holidays.desc: Residents craft lanterns out of lemons; children go door to door for lemon pastries; families gather to tell spooky stories around the citrus lanterns.

dishes.name: Vale Zest Bread
dishes.desc: Fragrant bread with candied lemon-peel bits.

dishes.name: Lemon Spark Ale
dishes.desc: Sparkling drink of fermented lemon juice with herbs.

streets.name: Zest Cellar Road
streets.desc: Stores candied lemon zest.

streets.name: Sourstone Alley
streets.desc: Walls said to be soaked in lemon scent.

cities.neighbors: The bright yellow valley between New Wobbleton and Buttonspire.

cities.name: Buttonspire
cities.desc: A town built around a tower studded with buttons, a symbol of prosperity since its founding. Losing a button means good luck; finding one means a new friend.

holidays.title: Festival of the Lost Button
holidays.desc: Residents wear clothes with deliberately mismatched buttons all day; in the evening they trade found buttons; the brighter the button, the more luck it brings.

dishes.name: Button Stew
dishes.desc: Hearty vegetable stew with button-shaped bread dumplings.

dishes.name: Threaded Pie
dishes.desc: Sweet pie with a lattice crust resembling stitched thread.

streets.name: Copper Button Alley
streets.desc: Lane of button craftsmen.

streets.name: Patchwork Square
streets.desc: Main square, named for its patchwork-style paving.

cities.neighbors: Below the Mountains of Buttons, just west of the Department of Reflection on the Deed.

cities.name: Noodleford
cities.desc: A noodle-obsessed town of steaming windows and lantern-strung dried noodles. Home to hundreds of noodle-house varieties; even weddings and funerals have their own noodle dishes.

holidays.title: Tanglefork Parade
holidays.desc: Giant figures made of noodles and sauce are paraded through the streets; residents throw fried noodles at each other like confetti.

holidays.title: Golden Broth Week
holidays.desc: Every street brews its own signature broth — mushroom, meat, vegetable, or spicy.

dishes.name: Brothmoon Soup
dishes.desc: Clear night broth with onion and egg.

dishes.name: Spicy Slurp Noodles
dishes.desc: Noodles in spicy sauce, impossible to eat quietly.

dishes.name: Sweet Sesame Tangles
dishes.desc: Sweet noodles with sesame and honey.

streets.name: Brothpot Lane
streets.desc: Street of broth-pot cooks.

streets.name: Tanglefork Square
streets.desc: Hosts the main festival.

cities.neighbors: Between Buttonspire, Kettleford, and Maplewink — the crossroads of the eastern isles.

cities.name: Jamshire
cities.desc: A jam-obsessed region where every household has a cellar of preserves, from strawberry to rhubarb-rose. "Having tea" locally means "gathering for a jar."

holidays.title: Festival of Sticky Fingers
holidays.desc: Children race to eat jam without a spoon; adults brew winter blends with cinnamon, clove, and orange.

holidays.title: Jam Jamboree
holidays.desc: A massive communal jam-making session on the main square using fruit brought by every resident.

holidays.title: Festival of Inkberries
holidays.desc: Residents gather ink-berries to make ink and jam, then write short poems on leaves hung from the trees.

dishes.name: Jamshire Layer Cake
dishes.desc: Layered cake with a different jam flavor in each layer.

dishes.name: Hot Berry Cider
dishes.desc: Warm cider made from apples and jam syrups.

dishes.name: Morning Jam Porridge
dishes.desc: Classic breakfast porridge topped with jam.

streets.name: Strawberry Spoon Street
streets.desc: Main pedestrian street, lined with tea houses.

streets.name: Raspberry Ripple Road
streets.desc: Jam is made with patterns swirled right in the jar.

streets.name: Apricot Glow Avenue
streets.desc: Smells of warm apricot jam in the evenings.

streets.name: Jelly Jar Square
streets.desc: Hosts the main festival.

cities.neighbors: Beside the Berry Fields, just south of Snailhollow and north of Cheddarford.

cities.name: Cheddarford
cities.desc: A river valley devoted to cheese, with caves used as natural aging cellars. Bridges are carved with wheel-of-cheese motifs.

holidays.title: Golden Grid Night
holidays.desc: Festive waffles with a golden cheese crust are baked; tradition is to count waffle squares instead of stars.

holidays.title: Bride & Bond Day
holidays.desc: Townsfolk braid a giant cheese braid for luck; couples exchange small cheese braids tied with red ribbon and hide wish-notes inside.

holidays.title: Aged Day
holidays.desc: Each family opens its oldest wheel of cheese; elders tell stories; "Century Secret" pies hide different cheeses inside; the young give the old "wisdom braids."

holidays.title: Golden Melt Festival
holidays.desc: Everyone dips bread, vegetables, or fruit into melted cheese; a contest for the longest cheese-string pull; the evening ends with "Melted Steps" dancing.

dishes.name: Cheddar Soup Bowl
dishes.desc: Thick soup served in a bread bowl with melted cheese.

dishes.name: River Crust Pie
dishes.desc: Pie with potato, onion, and melted cheddar.

dishes.name: Mature Ale
dishes.desc: Amber ale aged in the cheese caves.

dishes.name: Melted Bread Rolls
dishes.desc: Cheese-filled breakfast rolls.

dishes.name: Smoked Cheese Braids
dishes.desc: The town's signature dish.

dishes.name: Sweet Cheese-and-Honey Braids
dishes.desc: Symbolize "sweet love."

streets.name: Melted Wheel Road
streets.desc: Street of cheesemakers.

streets.name: Golden Melt Square
streets.desc: Site of the main festivals.

cities.neighbors: Straddles the river between Jamshire and Pinecrust.

cities.name: Kettleford
cities.desc: A town centered on tea and coffee culture, with a giant copper samovar and coffee cezve at its main square. Every household keeps at least three kettles and a copper cezve "just in case."

holidays.title: Great Whistle Day
holidays.desc: The whole town boils its kettles at once; the louder the collective whistle, the luckier the year.

holidays.title: Winter Brew Eve
holidays.desc: The town's main winter holiday — residents brew one giant communal pot of spiced tea for anyone who stops by.

dishes.name: Copper Roast Coffee
dishes.desc: Strong black coffee roasted and brewed only in copper cezves.

dishes.name: Honey Kettle Cakes
dishes.desc: Small honey cakes made for tea time.

dishes.name: Spiced Brew Duo
dishes.desc: Spiced apple-cider drink with a shot of espresso and tea infusion.

streets.name: Copper Steam Street
streets.desc: Home to samovar workshops and coffee roasters.

streets.name: Chamomile & Bean Court
streets.desc: Quiet spot for evening tea and coffee.

streets.name: Kettleclock Avenue
streets.desc: Its tower releases steam every hour to announce fresh brewing time.

cities.neighbors: South of Noodleford, across the water from Pinecrust and Maplewink.

cities.name: Department of Reflection on the Deed
cities.desc: A lone stone building on the road between Buttonspire and Noodleford, half prison, half filing office. Wrongdoers serve their sentence writing endless reflections until a confession finally rings true.

holidays.title: Confession Day
holidays.desc: Any inmate who writes a genuinely honest (or genuinely funny) confession gets a shot at early release; outside, islanders mail in mock "confessions" for their smallest sins, just for the joke of it.

dishes.name: Regret Stew
dishes.desc: A plain grey stew that locals swear tastes better the more honest you've been that day.

dishes.name: Ink-Black Tea
dishes.desc: Bitter, strong tea served to those writing long into the night.

streets.name: The Confession Hall
streets.desc: Main room where sentences are read aloud.

streets.name: The Ink Room
streets.desc: Where inmates write.

streets.name: The Long Corridor
streets.desc: Cells on either side.

streets.name: The Release Gate
streets.desc: The only door out.

cities.neighbors: Wedged on the road between Buttonspire and Noodleford — best visited briefly.
